subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: picks up tiny voltage fluctuations from the scalp without conductive gel.
parts: dry conductive pins or polymer tips

subsystems.name: Analog front end
subsystems.role: amplifies and digitises microvolt-level EEG while rejecting noise.

subsystems.name: Signal processing
subsystems.role: cleans the signal and extracts frequency-band power.

subsystems.name: Classification algorithm
subsystems.role: maps EEG features to a cognitive-load or exhaustion score.

subsystems.name: Power and wireless
subsystems.role: runs the headband and sends data to a phone or computer.

subsystems.name: User interface
subsystems.role: shows the user their mental state and alerts them.

buildSteps.title: Choose electrode sites
buildSteps.detail: Place dry electrodes over the prefrontal cortex (e.g., Fp1, Fp2, Fz) where theta and beta rhythms are measurable.

buildSteps.title: Make dry electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate pins or conductive polymer tips that part hair and maintain stable contact without gel.

buildSteps.title: Design the analog circuit
buildSteps.detail: Build a low-noise amplifier with high common-mode rejection and a band-pass filter (about 0.5–45 Hz).

buildSteps.title: Add digitisation and firmware
buildSteps.detail: Sample at 250–500 Hz, digitise, and stream data over Bluetooth.

buildSteps.title: Clean the signal
buildSteps.detail: Implement real-time removal of eye-blink and muscle artifacts using regression or independent component analysis.

buildSteps.title: Extract features
buildSteps.detail: Compute power in theta (4–8 Hz) and beta (13–30 Hz) bands and form the theta/beta ratio.

buildSteps.title: Train the classifier
buildSteps.detail: Collect EEG from volunteers performing tasks of varying difficulty, label with subjective or performance measures, and train a model to output a load score.

buildSteps.title: Validate against benchmarks
buildSteps.detail: Compare the score with established cognitive-load measures such as the NASA-TLX questionnaire or task performance.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and test
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the headband, app and alerts, then test for comfort, battery life and reliability in daily use.

prerequisites.why: allows long-term use without gel, though signal quality is lower than wet electrodes.
EEG signals are only tens of microvolts and easily buried in noise.
eye blinks and jaw clenches strongly contaminate prefrontal EEG and are hard to remove perfectly.
theta/beta ratio correlates with load in some studies but varies between people and tasks.
turns features into a usable score, but needs individual calibration.

pathway.milestone: research-grade EEG systems measure cognitive load in labs and simulators
pathway.unlocks: understanding of which EEG features track mental effort.

pathway.milestone: consumer headbands with validated load detection for specific tasks (e.g., air-traffic control, driving)
integration into workplace productivity tools and adaptive interfaces
pathway.unlocks: systems that adjust difficulty or schedule breaks automatically.
objective measures of fatigue in medicine and research.
